title: Vibraphone
reference_instrument: Iowa MIS vibraphone (model NA; the page states neither the bar alloy, the resonator geometry nor whether the fan motor ran). C4, E4 and A4 are compared with its sustained mf C4-B4 file; its pp and ff files give the ruler its other dynamic
summary: Three aluminium bars, C4, E4 and A4, each over its own resonator tube: not yet a vibraphone. Each bar is a builder's design in EN AW-2017A, its undercut solved in the engine so the first partial sits at equal temperament on A4 = 442 Hz with f2 = 4 f1, over the builder's as-built tube. The tube couples now that the bar's own radiation damping comes from the engine: each mode's radiated power from the boundary-element solve, added as max(W, 0) over a loss row measured with the air pumped out, so the air counts once. A negative W is below the solve's resolution and adds nothing; the floor it sets is 4.75e-3 per second on C4 and 3.48e-3 on E4, and on A4 no W comes out negative. Each tube's air column is read from the builder's CAD, to the floor face of its cup. The C4 tube's bore is read from it too, two printed parts with the narrowing ring where they join; the E4 tube, also two printed parts, keeps a uniform bore, its ring left out; and the A4 tube is one plain cylinder. With its tube C4's fundamental decays at 2.66 dB/s, just slower than the recording's 2.77 to 3.25, E4's at 4.50, still faster than the recording's 2.71 to 3.07, and A4's at 6.06, 1.7 to 2.2 times as fast as the recording's 2.80 to 3.58, where the C4 bar alone decayed four to five times slower. The bars are not the recording's instrument, and the rubber mallet is a stand-in.
physics_present: Three-dimensional bars with the C4, E4 and A4 outlines of a builder's F3-F6 vibraphone design (the Wyndorps DIY vibraphone pages: C4 323 x 57.15 x 12.0 mm, E4 303 x 50.8 x 12.0 mm, A4 277 x 44.45 x 12.0 mm, read from the builder's bar-set drawing), in EN AW-2017A aluminium with the Euralliage sheet's modulus, shear modulus, Poisson ratio and density, on a 56 x 6 x 3 mesh (A4 on 56 x 8 x 5)

A circular-arc undercut solved in the engine from the modes alone, for f1 at equal temperament on A4 = 442 Hz and f2 = 4 f1, the tuning rule a maker uses; 442 Hz is the tuning a maker prints for its M55-type vibraphones, and the grader's own read puts the recording's C4 to B4 within a few cents of it. The third mode is not aimed at

One loss factor on every bar mode, eta 8.340e-5, W. E. Howell's clean 2024-T4 aluminium beam 56 at 5.6e-4 atm (NASA TM X-2852, 1974): the beam's own loss with the air pumped out, from a thinner beam of a sister alloy, not a vibraphone bar

The bar's own radiation damping: each band mode's radiated power per unit modal velocity from the same Burton-Miller solve that gives the receiver, added to its loss as max(W, 0). Below the solve's resolution W comes out negative and adds nothing; the floor, the largest negative W, is printed beside the term: 4.75e-3 per second on C4 and 3.48e-3 on E4, where the third vertical modes' W are 4.35 and 11.1 per second; on A4 no W comes out negative, so the floor is 0, and the third vertical mode's W is 18.0 per second

The builder's resonator tube under each bar, a column closed at the bottom (bore and air column read from the builder's CAD parts: C4 radius 30.0 mm and air column 304.0 mm, E4 26.5 mm and 239.0 mm, each from the mouth to the floor face of the lower cup, whose floor is 2.0 mm thick, and A4 23.0 mm and 177.0 mm, one printed piece, a plain cylinder to its cup's 2.0 mm floor; on C4 the bore is the one drawn, its joint ring included, walked as plane waves with pressure and volume velocity continuous at each change of radius, and on E4 it is uniform at 26.5 mm), its modes coupled to the bar's modes through the bar's boundary elements and radiating from its mouth as a free compact source
A Hertz contact mallet, the marimba cards' hard rubber row (Chaigne and Doutaut 1997) at 1.0 m/s, a declared stand-in on aluminium
Burton-Miller boundary-element radiation from the bar up to the band the card states, with no box, heard through the broadband observer
physics_missing: The right decay: with its tube coupled, C4's fundamental decays at 2.66 dB/s (T60 22.6 s), just slower than the recording's 2.77 to 3.25 dB/s (T60 18 to 22 s, three strikes), E4's at 4.50 dB/s (T60 13.3 s), faster than the recording's 2.71 to 3.07 dB/s (two strikes), and A4's at 6.06 dB/s (T60 9.9 s), 1.7 to 2.2 times as fast as the recording's 2.80 to 3.58 dB/s (T60 17 to 21 s, three strikes). How much of the tube's loss each fundamental takes is set by how far the tube's first mode sits from it (with the bar's reflection in, 2.4 Hz above on C4, 2.3 Hz above on E4 and 3.1 Hz above on A4), by the tube's wall and open-end losses and by the bar-to-tube gap, which is not printed and is a 12.7 mm stand-in; the builder's frame CAD bounds it at 9 to 14 mm. Viscous air loss on the bar, the support cords and felts and the mallet's contact loss are not modelled, and nothing is adjusted to close the gap

The joint ring: where the two printed parts of the C4 and E4 tubes join (the A4 tube is one piece, with no ring), the lower part's ring narrows the bore over 12 mm (C4 to radius 27.9 mm, 48 to 60 mm above the floor face; E4 to 24.4 mm, 83 to 95 mm above it). On C4 the bore's plane-wave walk carries it and raises the tube's first mode by 0.95 Hz; at each change of radius only the plane wave is carried, so the inertance of the step's evanescent field and the loss on the step's annular face are left out. E4's playing render has a uniform bore and leaves the ring out, which a lossless transfer matrix over the CAD profile puts at +0.80 Hz on the tube's first mode

Radiation damping finer than the boundary-element solve resolves: a mode whose W comes out negative gets none, and the far-field radiated power is not computed. The modes the pages rest on sit well above the floor, except C4's 1051.3 Hz mode at 4.9 times it, which adds 0.20 dB/s to that partial's 2.60 dB/s
The recording's mallet: vibraphone mallets are usually cord- or yarn-wrapped and the recording names none; the hard rubber stand-in is not it
The fan valves that give the vibraphone its vibrato: not modelled. The recording's notes carry no envelope modulation at one rate common to all of them, so its motor was off
A measured vibraphone bar: the undercut is solved from the tuning rule, not measured, and the recording's bar alloy and outline are not stated
Neighbouring bars, the frame and the damper

A second take: the ruler compares the recording's other dynamics of the same note and its neighbouring notes, and has no other take of the note, since the Iowa page carries one take of each note at each dynamic
The recording's other notes from C4 to B4: only C4, E4 and A4 have cards
